thread:
oncall-bot: ALERT flood detected — 15 PD incidents opened in 3m for monitor `api-5xx-rate`. Suspected dupes from host-level grouping. Auto-escalation engaged.

alex: seeing the same. dashboards show a short spike from 18:22–18:25 UTC, mostly 502/504 from eu-west-1.

maya: are these new deploys? can we confirm customer impact first?

alex: no deploys on the schedule. sampling traces shows a surge of upstream timeouts to payment microservice. small subset of customers experienced errors (roughly 4% of traffic for a handful of routes). not a full outage.

sam: PD is spamming the oncall group because monitor is grouped by host. we should group by service+error-type instead to dedupe. changing monitor grouping now.

jen: recommend temporary throttling on PD alerts while we triage — set a 30m suppression on that monitor. i can create a silence. @maya do you want escalation paused?

maya: yes please pause escalation for the noisy monitor. we'll keep paging on critical-buckets only.

ops-bot: ACTION: alex to apply temporary monitor changes; jen to create PagerDuty suppression; sam to update dashboard panels.

alex: applying changes — switching Datadog monitor `api-5xx-rate` aggregation to `by {service, error_type}` and raising the alert threshold from `>0.5%` to `>1.5%` over 1m to avoid spikes. patch:```yaml
- monitor: api-5xx-rate
  query: "sum:requests.errors{*}.as_count() / sum:requests.count{*}.as_count() > 0.015"
  group_by: ["service","error_type"]
  evaluation_window: "1m"
```

alex: pushed the config. Datadog acknowledged, noise should drop in next minute.

jen: creating PD suppression (1h). PD API call:```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.pagerduty.com/alerts/silence" \
  -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service_ids":["P12345"], "duration":3600, "description":"Temporary suppression for noisy api-5xx-rate monitor"}'
```

jen: suppression created for 60m against service P12345. escalation paused.

sam: updating dashboards to add a rate-limited error panel and a per-region heatmap. will also add a small widget that shows active PD incidents for quick triage.

maya: confirmed customer impact: 4% error rate for ~7 minutes on several payment endpoints, highest in eu-west-1. CS pinged; no major revenue impact reported. we should run an RCA if root cause is upstream timeouts.

alex: digging into upstream logs; looks like a circuit breaker threshold in payment-fwd service tripped for a subset of backend hosts after a latency burst. restarting the 2 affected instances cleared the errors.

jen: restarting nodes was the right live mitigation. can we put a short-term autoscaling/CB tuning so it doesn't trip on transient blips?

alex: yes — filing an ops task to adjust CB backoff and add a slower ramp. assigning to sam for follow-up config changes.

ops-bot: NOTE: created ticket OP-4821 "tune payment-fwd circuit breaker ramp + dedupe alerts" assigned to sam, due 3 days.

maya: handoff for night oncall — @alex handing off to @maya: status — incident mitigated, suppression active for 60m, dashboard panels updated, OP-4821 created. please keep an eye on eu-west-1 error rate and PD quiet.

alex: handing off. key checks: error rate <1% for 10m window, no new PD incidents for the service, customer error tickets flagged in support queue. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/api-5xx-rate

maya: acknowledged. will monitor and escalate if it creeps back up.

jen: follow-up items for post-incident:
- convert monitor grouping to `service+error_type` permanently (no host grouping)
- add PD dedupe rules: group_by service + region tag
- add PD rate-limits for bursty monitors (30m window) and a playbook entry for temporary suppressions
- create a targeted dashboard for upstream timeout spike detection (alerts when backend latency > 750ms for 2m)

sam: i can take the first two and will open a PR this afternoon.

maya: thanks team. i'll write a short incident note and tag Customer Success. no immediate SLA breach. moving this thread to #postmortems once we have the RCA writeup. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: closed (mitigated) — 1813456789. PD suppression expires in 58m.

ops-bot: REMINDER: please add any overlooked actions to OP-4821 and link logs/traces before you go.

alex: one last note — consider adding a small debounce on the Datadog -> PD integration for this monitor (e.g., require two consecutive evals to fire). that would have prevented the flood.

jen: noted, adding to the playbook.

maya: thanks all, signing off in 15.
